design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (cpi_insurance_verification_and_force_placement), round 10

[Draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [4, 4, 6]: cpi_ext_feed_proof_rereview 6, cpi_ext_upload_proof_rereview 4, cpi_ext_closing_month_refund 4 (root, owner=user).

[Test] The borrower paid off by wire on 2026-08-05 and asks for the force-placed premium for the time she had her own insurance back, by check. The closing-month refund is fixed only after / not until the records carry accepted re-reviews of every rejected insurer-feed proof and every rejected uploaded binder reaching the refunded period. Both proofs start inside the latest charge's period (Pecos Valley binder 2026-07-06..07-11 by upload; Gulf Coast month-to-month policy 2026-07-18..08-18 by feed), list the company as lienholder and were first rejected for deductibles above the Plan B maximum of 500.00. The agent re-reviews each under the written acceptance schedule, then refunds the unearned premium.

[Refund content] Unearned premium only, earned by actual days: the period's capitalised premium times refundable days over the period days. Basis pro_rata_from_proof_effective. Refundable days = the union of the two spans plus the first days of the replacement gap, as many as the book-value, state and model-year allowances add up to; the charge has no post-closing days. Standard method (the base proof basis): days from the latest reaching proof's effective date through the closed date, no grace. No interest, fee or credit.

[One refundable charge] No accepted proof reaches any earlier charge (both start on or after 2026-07-06, the latest period's start; the original 2025 proof expired before the placement), so the kept base rule owes nothing on any other charge, and this refund is everything the rules leave refundable.

[Tree] Root closing-month refund; value_input edges to the feed and upload re-reviews (state form). Only the feed re-review writes accepted insurer_edi_feed entries and only the upload re-review writes accepted declarations_page_upload entries. Opening falsity: both entries carry rejected_deductible_too_high. The re-reviews commute.

[Base] Re-review rules govern closed records only (open records keep the base review and lifecycle); refunds read accepted proofs of every channel alike, and their hand-off of the latest charge is conditioned on an accepted proof counting for it and the plain record test that no verification_source holds more than one accepted proof entry (otherwise the base refund rule, restated and computed as written). Re-reviews retire, for refund-only re-reviews on a closed record, the open-record gate, the policy-on-file update and the deductible and expiration clauses; policies also retire the binder clause; the upload rule re-reviews only binders. Refund retires the pro-rata-from-proof and closure clauses for the charge ending on the closed date; the three bases stay base for every other charge; destination mailed_to_borrower.

[Factors] Re-reviews: model-year, loan-to-value (policies), book-value and credit-tier allowances, reach date by record status (method), state expiry buffer (policies). Refund: coverage-span counting (method), replacement-grace allowances by book value, contract state and model year. Each factor's solo standard substitution changes the scored value (computations.factor_sensitivity).

[Seed] Contract inside Tier 5 limits (54 months, 13,600.00 on 11,900.00 book = 114.3 %), wire payoff 2026-08-05. CPI history: original proof accepted 2025-08-20 (confirmed by the borrower's agent by phone), lapse 2026-02-15, notices 2026-02-18 / 03-05, placement 2026-04-06 effective 2026-03-07, five charges, binder rejected 2026-07-08 and feed policy rejected 2026-08-04 with deficient-proof notices, record closed 2026-08-05.

[Persona] States the payoff and her own coverage start dates, asks for the check; identity on request; agrees to reviews; runs the hand-over with whatever figure.

[Probe table] plan.md "Round 6 probe table".
user_scenario: You are Marisol Quintero, 35, a dental office manager in Dallas, Texas. You are calm, organised and a little tired of paperwork, and you speak in plain, friendly sentences. In August you refinanced your 2019 Nissan Altima with your credit union, which wired Harborline the payoff on August 5 and closed your contract with them. Looking at the payoff statement afterwards you saw that Harborline had kept adding force-placed insurance to the loan all spring and summer. You did get your own insurance back in July: first a short binder from Pecos Valley Insurance Company that started July 6, and then a month-to-month policy with Gulf Coast Casualty Company that started July 18. You open the call by saying you paid off your car loan in August and you want back whatever force-placed insurance you were charged for the time you had your own insurance, sent to you as a check at the address they have on file; you want it taken care of on this call, and you are happy for the representative to handle whatever is needed on their side. You do not know any amounts, charge dates or internal statuses and you do not guess them; if asked what you expect, you say you want them to work it out from their records. Only when the representative asks how to find you, you give your phone number, 2145550121. Only when asked to verify, you give your date of birth, 1991-04-23, and your ZIP code, 75217; if they need more, the last four of your Social Security number are 2417 and your email is marisol.quintero@outlook.com. If asked for your account number you read it from an old statement: 7220014583. If the representative asks whether they may review or record anything on your insurance file to sort out the refund, you say yes, please go ahead. If they ask where the refund should go, a check to 4418 Bonnie View Rd, Dallas, TX 75217 is fine. When the representative tells you the refund amount and hands you the step to request the check yourself, you run it with exactly what they give you, whatever the figure. Once you hear that the refund check has been issued, you thank them and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount_usd: 77.27. Premium 79.85 for 2026-07-06..2026-08-05 (31 days), closed 2026-08-05. No post-closing days. Refundable 25 + 5 = 30. 79.85 x 30 / 31 rounded half-up -> 77.27.

edges.condition: cpi_activities carries, on the tracking record, an accepted cpi_proof_verified entry from insurer_edi_feed for every rejected proof of that channel whose shown coverage reaches into the billing period of the most recent capitalised premium charge.
edges.policy_source: The closing-month refund is fixed only after the records carry an accepted re-review of every rejected insurer-feed proof whose shown coverage reaches into that billing period.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The only insurer_edi_feed proof reaching into the latest charge's billing period is rejected and has no accepted re-review.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: rereview_feed_proof_7d2611c6 writes an accepted cpi_proof_verified entry copying that proof.

edges.condition: cpi_activities carries, on the tracking record, an accepted cpi_proof_verified entry from declarations_page_upload for every rejected uploaded binder (shown period no longer than binder_max_days) whose shown coverage reaches into the billing period of the most recent capitalised premium charge.
edges.policy_source: The closing-month refund is not fixed until the records carry an accepted re-review of every rejected uploaded binder whose shown coverage reaches into that billing period.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two re-reviews write separate entries for different source proofs and neither reads the other's channel; either order gives the same rows and refund; the refund follows both, as its two prerequisite sentences state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the feed re-review only the binder reaches the period and amount_usd falls from 77.27 to 15.45.
Without the upload re-review only the feed policy reaches the period and amount_usd falls from 77.27 to 48.94.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never mentions a rejected proof, a deficient-proof letter or a review; she states the payoff and her own coverage start dates and asks for the refund by check; she only agrees if asked whether her insurance file may be reviewed.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: The refund tool writes whatever charge and amount it is given; the re-review tools record whatever outcome they are given; none checks a prerequisite or refuses.
